claims.statement: The pyaudiocast package re-exports exactly AudioPlayer, __version__, list_output_devices and play_file from the native module pyaudiocast._pyaudiocast, which registers them at module initialization.
pyaudiocast.__version__ is the Cargo package version compiled into the extension.
list_output_devices() returns one dict per device with name, id, index (the position in the returned list) and type keys, and enumerates devices without holding the GIL.
Listed device ids are unique: cpal devices report their bare device id with the host id as type, and PipeWire/PulseAudio sinks are appended with id 'pipewire:<sink>' and type 'pipewire'.
AudioPlayer raises ValueError unless sample_rate is within 1000..=768000 Hz and channels within 1..=64; None adopts the device's default rate or channel count.
The sample_rate and channels properties report the caller's audio format, while device_sample_rate and device_channels report the configuration the device stream was opened with.

write() accepts bytes and bytearray as int16 little-endian PCM, list[float], and numpy int16/int32/float32/float64 arrays that are 1-D interleaved or 2-D shaped (frames, channels) with channels equal to the player's channel count; other inputs raise TypeError and mis-shaped arrays raise ValueError.
write() blocks while the ring buffer, which holds four seconds of device-format audio, is full.
write() chunks may end mid-sample or mid-frame; the remainder is completed by the next write unless a drain() or clear() ended the stream first, in which case it is dropped.
Float samples from lists and float numpy arrays are clamped to -1.0..MAX_SAMPLE and non-finite values are replaced with silence.

drain() waits until the audio written before the call has been consumed by the audio callback and has become audible, ignores audio written after it started, and returns without error if clear() or stop() intervenes or already happened.
clear() discards buffered audio, causes an in-flight write() to drop its remaining data and return normally, and unblocks a pending drain().
stop() is idempotent and closes the player: later writes, and writes blocked when it runs, raise RuntimeError 'Stream error: Player is closed'.
is_active is True only while the player has not been stopped and its stream has not failed.
Using AudioPlayer as a context manager returns the player itself and calls stop() on exit.
Every SpeakerError is raised in Python as RuntimeError whose message starts with 'Device not found:', 'No default output device available', 'Stream error:', 'Config error:' or 'IO error:'.
Blocking write(), drain() and play_file() run Python signal handlers about every 100 ms while waiting, so Ctrl+C raises KeyboardInterrupt promptly.
play_file() accepts a str or path-like, opens the player at the WAV file's sample rate and channel count, and blocks until playback has drained.
play_file() plays files that end before their declared length without raising, and raises other decode errors only after playing the audio that decoded.

AudioPlayer methods may be called from other threads or from signal handlers while a write() is blocked, because the class is a frozen pyclass with mutex/atomic state and write() does not hold the writer lock while waiting.
write() takes the writer lock separately for conversion and for each ring-buffer push step, so concurrent write() calls from several threads are not serialized as whole chunks.
numpy is optional: arrays are only inspected once numpy is present in sys.modules, and bytes/list input works with the numpy import blocked.
Stream failures are latched: once the stream has failed, write() and drain() raise RuntimeError carrying the first failure message.

Release 0.2.0 changed observable behavior: type reports the real host, sink ids became 'pipewire:<sink>', write() accepts unaligned chunks instead of raising ValueError, drain()/clear() end the stream, play_file raises decode errors after playing, and macOS streams keep the device's rate and channel count.
